text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bodies of seven persons who drowned at Lagos beach on New Year's Day washed ashore.
- Banks shun Central Bank's offer to them to trade in securities among themselves.
- Afribank, the fourth biggest bank in Nigeria, appoints two new executive directors.
- Head of security at airport in northern Kaduna arrested and airport sources say this may be over an uncovered plot to bomb the facility.
- In a survey ahead of release of Nigeria's fiscal 1997 budget, economists suggest that measures be taken by the government to boost the value of the naira currency against convertible currencies.

- Banking sector supervisor Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) appeals against a Failed Bank's Tribunal ruling which cleared the deposed Sultan of Sokoto Ibrahim Dasuki of fraud allegations.
- French Embassy in Lagos says it will now accept only 50 naira currency notes from visa applicants.
- Former Nigerian military ruler Ibrahim Babangida returns home from France after a successful operation on his foot.
